caption_hook: New Mexico has been a coastal swamp, a tropical reef and a rift valley with supervolcanoes.

layers.name: BANDELIER TUFF
layers.what: Two giant eruptions in the Jemez Mountains spread hot ash across the region and left the Valles Caldera. The ash welded into soft tuff, hundreds of feet thick.
layers.bonus: Ancestral Puebloans carved homes and cave rooms right into the cliffs at Bandelier.

layers.name: FRUITLAND FORMATION
layers.what: Along the edge of a retreating sea, swamps built up plant material that became coal. Wind and rain now carve the soft layers into hoodoos and strange mushroom shapes.
layers.bonus: Bisti and De-Na-Zin badlands are sculpted from it and its neighbors.

layers.name: CHINLE FORMATION
layers.hook: Dinosaur pack in the red mud
layers.what: Colorful mudstones record rivers and floodplains early in the Age of Dinosaurs. At Ghost Ranch, hundreds of small Coelophysis dinosaurs were buried together.
layers.bonus: Coelophysis, a speedy little hunter, became New Mexico's state fossil in 1981.

layers.name: CAPITAN LIMESTONE
layers.hook: A reef you can walk through
layers.what: A giant horseshoe-shaped reef grew in a warm sea. Acid-rich water later dissolved caves into the limestone, and uplift raised the whole reef into the Guadalupe Mountains.
layers.bonus: Carlsbad Caverns holds a cave room called the Big Room, nearly 4,000 feet long.

layers.name: MADERA LIMESTONE
layers.hook: Sea shells on a mountain crest
layers.what: A shallow sea covered this region, building thick beds of gray limestone full of shells, corals and sea lilies. Uplift later raised them high above the valley.
layers.bonus: It caps the Sandia Mountains above Albuquerque, over 10,000 feet up.

layers.name: THE BASEMENT
layers.hook: Granite and gneiss under it all
layers.what: The oldest rocks in New Mexico are granite, gneiss and schist that formed deep in the crust. They form the bones of the Sandia and Sangre de Cristo ranges.
layers.bonus: Wheeler Peak, 13,161 ft and the state's highest summit, stands on Precambrian rock.
